[[File:Barrett O'Neill 1980 (portioned).jpg|thumb|upright|Barrett O'Neill in 1980]]
'''Barrett O'Neill''' (1924– 16 June 2011) was an American mathematician.<ref name="legacy.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/latimes/obituary.aspx?n=barrett-oneill&pid=152162811&fhid=11022|title=Barrett O'NEILL's Obituary on Los Angeles Times|work=legacy.com|accessdate=30 March 2017}}</ref> He is known for contributions to [[differential geometry]], including two widely-used textbooks on its foundational theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/news/memoriam-barrett-oneill-professor-mathematics-emeritus-1924-%E2%80%93-2011|title=In memoriam: Barrett O'Neill Professor of Mathematics, Emeritus, 1924 – 2011 – UCLA Department of Mathematics|work=ucla.edu|accessdate=2022-11-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330090005/https://www.math.ucla.edu/news/memoriam-barrett-oneill-professor-mathematics-emeritus-1924-%E2%80%93-2011|archive-date=2017-03-30}}</ref> He was the author of eighteen research articles, the last of which was published in 1973.

He received his Ph.D. in mathematics in 1951 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. His doctoral advisor was [[Witold Hurewicz]]. His dissertation thesis was titled ''Some Fixed Point Theorems''<ref name="nodak.edu">{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=13232|title=Barrett O'Neill – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|work=nodak.edu|accessdate=30 March 2017}}</ref> He has worked as a professor of mathematics at [[UCLA]], where he supervised the PhDs of eight doctoral students.<ref name="nodak.edu"/>

He made a foundational contribution to the theory of [[Riemannian submersion]]s, showing how geometric quantities on the total space and on the base are related to one another. "O'Neill's formula" refers to the relation between the [[sectional curvature]]s. O'Neill's calculations simplified earlier work by other authors, and have become standard textbook material.<ref>Peter Petersen. ''Riemannian geometry.'' Third edition. Graduate Texts in Mathematics, 171. Springer, Cham, 2016. xviii+499 pp. {{ISBN|978-3-319-26652-7|978-3-319-26654-1}}</ref> With [[Richard L. Bishop|Richard Bishop]], he applied his submersion calculations to the geometry of [[warped geometry|warped products]], in addition to studying the fundamental role of convex functions and convex sets in [[Riemannian geometry]], and for the geometry of negative [[sectional curvature]] in particular. An article with his former Ph.D. student Patrick Eberlein made a number of further contributions to the Riemannian geometry of negative curvature, including the notion of the "boundary at infinity".

== Major publications ==
'''Books'''
* Barrett O'Neill. ''Elementary differential geometry.'' Revised second edition of the 1966 original. Elsevier/Academic Press, Amsterdam, 2006. xii+503 pp. {{ISBN|978-0-12-088735-4|0-12-088735-5}}
* Barrett O'Neill. ''Semi-Riemannian geometry. With applications to relativity.'' Pure and Applied Mathematics, 103. Academic Press, Inc. [Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, Publishers], New York, 1983. xiii+468 pp. {{ISBN|0-12-526740-1}}
* Barrett O'Neill. ''The geometry of Kerr black holes.'' A K Peters, Ltd., Wellesley, MA, 1995. xviii+381 pp. {{ISBN|1-56881-019-9}}
'''Articles'''
* Barrett O'Neill. ''The fundamental equations of a submersion.'' Michigan Math. J. 13 (1966), 459–469. {{doi|10.1307/mmj/1028999604}} {{free access}} 
* R.L. Bishop and B. O'Neill. ''Manifolds of negative curvature.'' Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 145 (1969), 1–49. {{doi|10.2307/1995057}} {{closed access}}; {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9947-1969-0251664-4}} {{free access}}
* P. Eberlein and B. O'Neill. ''Visibility manifolds.'' Pacific J. Math. 46 (1973), 45–109. {{doi|10.2140/pjm.1973.46.45}} {{free access}}
